quote: To offset the the bill and, charge electric, vehicle.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers an EV charging use case unprompted, which signals higher electric load and a stronger case for system sizing conversation at the appointment. EV load isn't in Ion's documented cross-sell catalog, but it is a concrete usage-growth signal the schema's interest_in_solar item flags as worth expanding on.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to reflect this back ('so between the house and the car, your usage is probably climbing') to build curiosity about sizing rather than letting it pass as a one-line answer.

quote: How do I know that? Probably yes. Because, some time ago, they replaced, not replaced. I don't know. Maybe they replaced them so that they can check them, remotely.
stewart_read: The customer gives an uncertain, rambling answer about whether he has his own power meter, and the rep accepts it at face value ('Okay. Cool. Yeah. You should be golden then.') without any further confirmation. This is a soft verify item left unresolved rather than a hard DQ risk, but it's a real gap in confirmation discipline.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the meter detail as something the site-visit specialist will physically confirm anyway, making the loose pass-through low-stakes rather than a genuine miss.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to either ask one clarifying follow-up or explicitly note the uncertainty for the closer/specialist rather than converting an unclear answer into a confident 'you should be golden.'

quote: And then how much do you pay a month on average?
stewart_read: Rep captures the bill figure directly and promptly, hitting the required verify item within about two minutes of the interest question.
coaching_implication: Capture itself is solid; the miss is what happens next — see the bill_anchor_audit for the flip gap.

quote: You can use 150 as a benchmark. I I can send you the bill so that you can see how it changes to the year.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a bill number and even volunteers that the bill fluctuates seasonally, an anchor-ready detail. The rep replies 'Cool. Yeah. Let me shoot you a text so you can send a bill,' moving straight into bill-collection logistics without reflecting the number back or connecting it to pain.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have deliberately deferred any bill discussion to the specialist's on-site design conversation, treating the setter's job as collection-only rather than persuasion.
coaching_implication: Show the rep the moment where a one-line reflection ('$150 with it climbing seasonally — that's real money to lock in') would have created pull without adding scope creep.

quote: Yeah. Yeah. I mean, we we do have a drone. We use it sometimes.
stewart_read: Customer asks an operational/technical question about how the roof will be assessed given its height. The rep answers with specific equipment detail (drone use) rather than deflecting to the specialist, which is minor but is exactly the kind of operational content the schema flags as premature.
alternative_hypothesis: The answer is short, low-stakes, and resolves a legitimate logistics worry (will someone actually be able to see the roof) rather than pitching product, so it may not rise to a coaching-worthy scope violation.
coaching_implication: Not urgent on its own, but worth naming as a pattern to watch — the rep is comfortable answering operational specifics live instead of using the escape hatch.

quote: Okay. Perfect. K. Alright. Well, you have a good one. Bye.
stewart_read: The appointment day and time are locked, but the call ends without the hour-block statement, the no-driving/computer instruction, or an explicit 'is that fair?' handshake. The schema directly ties these missing elements to higher no-show rates.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always run the full button-up checklist even on an easy, cooperative call — the ease of this booking likely caused the rep to skip steps that matter most for show-rate protection.

quote: Is there anyone else on the title of the home with you?
stewart_read: Rep correctly asks the co-owner question and the customer confirms his wife is on the title, but she is never mentioned again — not invited to the appointment, not flagged for the closer.
alternative_hypothesis: In-person specialist visits may inherently expect both homeowners present since it's a home visit rather than a phone call, softening the need for an explicit spoken invitation.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to explicitly confirm the wife will be present for the in-home appointment rather than assuming it by default — this is a booked-but-structurally-incomplete pattern the schema flags as a paycheck risk (fragile sit).

quote: How do you do it? Because you said the credit score is important. So so you do financing or or what?
stewart_read: Post-booking, the customer asks a real financing question. The rep answers briefly and defers to the specialist rather than diving into program specifics, which is a defensible, scope-disciplined response rather than a genuine miss.
alternative_hypothesis: A stricter read would call this curiosity_creation_failure for not converting the question into anticipation for the appointment, but the rep's brevity and clean redirect are closer to correct procedure than to a coaching failure.
coaching_implication: No urgent action needed; use as a positive contrast if coaching the rep's incentives-question deflection at 08:17.
